# Angles and trigonometry. An Angle knows its unit, so sin() can never be handed degrees by mistake.
from math import Angle, deg, rad, turn, grad, sin, cos, tan, atan2, hypot, sqrt, pi

def round3(x: float) -> float:
    return int(x * 1000 + 0.5) / 1000

def heading(dx: float, dy: float) -> Angle:
    # the direction of (dx, dy), measured from the x axis; atan2 takes y first and works out the quadrant
    return atan2(dy, dx)

@main
def main():
    # four ways to make an angle, each printing in its own unit
    a = deg(90)
    print(a, rad(1.5), turn(0.25), grad(100))
    # the same right angle in every unit
    print(a.deg(), a.rad(), a.turn(), a.grad())
    print(a == turn(0.25), a == grad(100), deg(45) < rad(1))
    # arithmetic keeps the unit on the left
    print(deg(90) + deg(45), deg(90) + turn(0.25), deg(30) * 3, deg(90) / 4)
    # trigonometry takes an Angle; the exact quarter turns are exact
    print(sin(deg(90)), cos(deg(90)), cos(deg(180)))
    print(round3(sin(deg(30))), round3(cos(deg(60))), round3(tan(deg(45))))
    # going back: asin, acos, atan and atan2 give an Angle
    print(atan2(1, 1), atan2(1, 1).deg())
    print(heading(-3.0, 3.0).deg(), heading(3.0, -3.0).deg())
    # angles wrap round
    print(deg(370).normalized(), deg(270).signed(), turn(2.25).normalized())
    # a point on a circle of radius 5, 30 degrees round from the x axis
    r = 5.0
    t = deg(30)
    x = r * cos(t)
    y = r * sin(t)
    print(round3(x), round3(y), round3(hypot(x, y)), round3(sqrt(x * x + y * y)))
    print(round3(rad(pi).deg()))
